title: Governor's Island memories and Jim and Andy's
summary: The band's move to Staten Island, a final ceremony at Governor's Island, and going to Jim and Andy's with Igoe to meet Jake Hanna and Joe Jones.

blocks.x: But I played the final ceremony there, and then I took that picture, and now in the bookshop and when you get off you see the whole history of Governor’s Island, but I’m © Fillius Jazz Archive -17-

one of the last guys from the Army that was there. But then we were transferred over the Staten Island and we were the first Army band, which is in that picture with me in front of the barracks. And then once the first Army was transferred down to Fort Monroe, Virginia, the second Army because the first Army and we became the New York Army Band. So that was the New York Army Band. But I would get the Staten Island Ferry and go see Sonny. But he would schedule the lessons so it would be the last lesson of the day, you know, so I would go in the afternoon and then he and I would together go over to Jim and Andy’s, which was a popular jazz hangout for every band, and he would introduce me to Jake Hanna, Joe Jones.

He was doing the “Merv Griffin Show” I think. Yeah, that was a classic hangout where if you were looking for a musician just call downstairs, “we need a trumpet player” up in such-and-such a studio. But that was, so anyway, Sonny and I became really good friends. And he still owes me, even to this day, he owes me one lesson, because I got transferred to Korea. Now here’s what happened with that. I mean was there something that you wanted to know a little bit more about the Army?
